correctness.rationale: The exact one-positive section ratio follows by conditioning the exponential representation of the regular-simplex section density on its unique positive summand. Every normal at fixed spherical angle from the facet normal is parameterized by a zero-sum unit tangent vector with first coordinate zero. The remaining optimization is exact: for the logarithm of each positive product factor, the third derivative is negative; the quadratic Hermite interpolant at the lower coordinate bound b and the repeated candidate r gives f<=Q coordinatewise. Because Q is quadratic, its sum is fixed by the zero first moment and unit second moment, proving the claimed product maximum. Equality in the Hermite remainder forces coordinates in {b,r}, and the zero-sum constraint forces exactly one b. Direct substitution gives the displayed profile and checking the equality geodesic's coordinates gives the stated angular endpoint. The finite verifier reproduces equality and random interior inequalities for dimensions 3 through 10, but the proof does not rely on those samples.

originality.rationale: The closest prior result located is the public finding 'Quantitative stability and exact Hessian for minimal central simplex sections', which proves only the chamber bound the secant angular lower bound, a low-sublevel global stability threshold, and the Hessian. The 2026 Ambrus--Gargyan paper proves the global minimum and equality orbit but not a fixed-angle radial envelope. König and Dirksen provide section formulas and earlier local/partial extremal information without the present sharp constrained product optimization. The new profile is strictly larger than sec(theta) for every positive angle in its range and has a fully classified equality orbit, so it is not a restatement or special case of the checked statements.
residual_risks: The lead global-minimum theorem is very recent, so a simultaneous or not-yet-indexed fixed-angle refinement could exist.
The constrained product lemma may appear independently in inequality literature under a different moment-problem formulation, though targeted equivalent-form searches did not locate such coverage.

value.rationale: The exact fixed-angle envelope is a natural quantitative invariant of the newly resolved minimum problem. It replaces a nonsharp chamber stability inequality by the best possible finite-angle bound, identifies every equality direction, and supplies genuinely nonlinear information beyond the already known Hessian. This is useful for sharp near-extremal analysis and is not an arbitrary finite computation or routine parameter substitution.
